body:
Static styling is not a UI — ship the interaction states, and VERIFY them by driving a real mouse.

The set that reads as "modern power-user" and that Aman called out as missing: row hover tint plus the same tint on focus-within; secondary row actions revealed with opacity (never `hidden`, which reflows the list under the cursor) on group-hover AND group-focus-within; the primary action always visible, because a list whose main action only appears on hover is awkward on a trackpad; real tooltips on icon-only controls instead of native `title` (native waits ~1s, cannot be styled, never shows on keyboard focus — the control is effectively unlabelled); chevrons that rotate rather than swap glyphs; a keyboard cursor drawn as a left rule so selection never shifts layout; active:translate-y-px press on buttons.

How to verify, since unit tests assert content and callbacks, not geometry or interaction: open the built surface over CDP, dispatch a real Input.dispatchMouseEvent mouseMoved over the row, and read getComputedStyle back — opacity 0 idle, 1 on hover, 1 after .focus(); row background changes; tooltip element has text. A screenshot alone proves none of this.
